newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakh factory bosses told - sell cars to pay wages.
newsitem.headline: Kazakh factory bosses told - sell cars to pay wages.

text.p: A regional boss in the icy north of Kazakhstan has urged the heads of its rustbelt factories to sell their own cars to help cover a dizzying backlog of unpaid wages, the daily Karavan Blitz said on Thursday.
Kazhmurad Nagmanov is "akim", or head, of the Eastern Kazakhstan region, home to a polluting and debt-ridden collection of uranium, lead and zinc plants bordering Russia.
Nagmanov is pushing to have wages paid on time but the newspaper said acidly there was as yet no word that "any of the directors were rushing to take the akim's advice".

The transition to a market economy has impoverished a large slice of the former Soviet republic's 16.9 million population, with many families unable to buy enough to eat. Energy shortages also mean a bitter cold winter in the republic which, ironically, is rich in oil and gas.
